strings.name: Ekrem İmamoğlu
strings.role: Turkish opposition politician and suspended elected mayor of Istanbul
strings.summary: Ekrem İmamoğlu rose from mayor of Beylikdüzü district to mayor of Istanbul, winning two mayoral votes in 2019 and re-election in 2024. He was detained and suspended in 2025, then left the Republican People’s Party and joined Yeni Parti in 2026. His municipal record, presidential candidacy claims and legal situation remain prominent issues.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026. November reports still described him as detained while the corruption trial continued. A separate party-congress criminal case was scheduled for a hearing on the 18th; that day’s outcome was not verified in this review. Prosecutors’ sentencing requests, administrative suspension and final convictions are distinguished. Party support does not establish legal eligibility for a presidential election.
strings.influence.rationale: His rise from Istanbul’s municipal government made him a major opposition figure whose elections and legal situation attract international attention.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education and the diploma dispute
strings.facts.f1.value: He graduated in business administration from Istanbul University in 1994 and later completed master’s studies in human resource management there. In 2025, the university separately annulled his undergraduate and master’s graduation status and diplomas. He challenged these decisions in court; older biographies alone do not establish the current status of those qualifications.
strings.facts.f2.label: From business to local politics
strings.facts.f2.value: Born in Akçaabat, Trabzon province, in 1970, he began working in the family construction business in 1992 and also participated in sports-club administration. He joined the Republican People’s Party in 2008 and subsequently developed his local political career in Beylikdüzü.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Municipal elections and national influence
strings.highlights.h1.text: His 2019 victory ended roughly 25 years of rule in Istanbul by the Justice and Development Party and its predecessors. Winning again in 2024 increased his national prominence, but a local election victory is not a presidential victory, and party backing cannot replace statutory candidacy requirements.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Detention and judicial independence
strings.highlights.h2.text: He denies the corruption allegations and calls the case politically motivated. Human-rights organisations questioned his detention and judicial independence in a 2026 third-party submission to the European Court of Human Rights. This is the interveners’ position, not a judgment already delivered by that court.
strings.timeline.t1.title: New phase in the municipal corruption trial
strings.timeline.t1.text: Proceedings resumed with witness testimony after he completed a round of defence on 17 October. The release of other defendants did not mean his release. The contemporaneous party-congress voting prosecution is a separate case, adjourned on 11 November to the 18th.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Leaving the CHP and moving to Yeni Parti
strings.timeline.t2.text: Through his presidential candidacy office, he announced his resignation and support for Yeni Parti, led by Özgür Özel. A report on the 14th quoted the provincial party chair confirming that he had become its first member in Istanbul. The statement on the 12th and subsequent membership reporting are separate events.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Remanded in custody and suspended as mayor
strings.timeline.t3.text: After being taken into custody on 19 March, he was remanded on the 23rd, when the Interior Ministry described his suspension as a temporary measure. The CHP primary backed his presidential candidacy that day. This party process was neither a presidential election nor a verdict in the corruption case.
strings.timeline.t4.title: University annuls undergraduate diploma
strings.timeline.t4.text: The university cancelled his undergraduate qualification over alleged irregularities in his 1990 transfer, then annulled his master’s qualification on 24 July. A related administrative action was dismissed in January 2026; March reporting concerned another refusal of a request to suspend execution. The administrative dispute is not itself a criminal conviction for document forgery.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Re-elected mayor of Istanbul
strings.timeline.t5.text: He defeated Justice and Development Party candidate Murat Kurum and gained a new municipal mandate. This was part of nationwide local elections, distinct from Türkiye’s 2023 presidential election.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Winning the rerun
strings.timeline.t6.text: After the previous result was annulled, he contested the rerun and increased his winning margin. He received his election certificate and resumed office on 27 June. Polling day and the formal resumption of office are different dates.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First victory in Istanbul’s mayoral election
strings.timeline.t7.text: He won as the CHP candidate and began serving on 17 April after a recount. On 6 May, the Supreme Electoral Council annulled the result and ordered a rerun. This brief tenure is recorded separately from his return to office in June.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Elected mayor of Beylikdüzü
strings.timeline.t8.text: He won the local election and served as district mayor until 2019. Beylikdüzü is a district of Istanbul; this office is distinct from the citywide metropolitan mayoralty.
